Name: Striped Skunk - Mephitis mephitis
Habitat: Open country, mixed woods, brushland, prairie prefered. Mainly nocturnal.
Foods: Mostly animal. Insects, spiders, toads, frogs, lizards, mice, gophers, turtle eggs, birds, fleshy fruits, grasses.
Name: Coyote - Canis latrans
Habitat: No boundaries. Prefers areas where cover is readily available such as brush, boulders, ravines.
Foods: Wide variety of plants and animals. Small mammals to deer, sheep, fleshy fruits, carrion, etc.
Miscellaneous: Valuable pelts during winter. Blamed for high mortality to domestic stock and wild population.
Name: Red Fox - Vulpes fulva
Habitat: brushy areas where escape cover is available, will nunt in open. Mostly nocturnal.
Foods: Mainly animal. Mice, other small rodents, rabbits, birds, frogs, insects, carrion, various fruits and berries.
Miscellaneous: May cause damage to domestic and wild fowl. Pelt is valuable.
Name: Swift fox - Vulpes velox
Habitat: Open areas; sandy, plains, low vegetation. Mostly nocturnal.
Foods: Small rodents, rabbits.
Miscellaneous: Few in number in U.S. of special concern to conservationists.
Name: Bobcat - Lynx rufus
Habitat: Areas where cover is available (secretive). From deserts to mountains, rimrock areas are prefered.
Foods: Small mammals, birds, occasionally deer.
Miscellaneous: Valued for its winter pelt.
Name: Blacktailed Prairie Dog - Cynomys <u>ludovicianus</u>
Habitat: High, dry, plains, praires. Live in communities
called "towns".
Foods: Predominately plants. Occasionally insects. Almost any green vegetation, wheatgrass, Russian thistle, fescue, bluegrass, grama, barley, saltbush, globe mallow, plantain, sunflower.
Name: Red Squirrel - Tamiascivrus hudsonicus
Habitat: Pine or spruce forests.
Foods: Insects, young birds, eggs, fresh carrion, couifer seeds, fleshy fruits, nuts.
